issues.legal_issue: A person resisting delivery of immovable property in execution may have the resistance adjudicated even if that person is not bound by the decree or asserts an independent right.
material_facts: A final decree for possession was being executed.
A person who was not a judgment-debtor obstructed delivery of possession.
The obstruction was not shown to arise from a right derived from the judgment-debtor.
issues.conclusion: The summary delivery procedure under Order 21, Rule 35(3) applies only where the person in possession is bound by the decree. Under Order 21, Rule 97, the executing court may enquire into resistance by any person, including one asserting a right independent of the judgment-debtor.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21, Rule 35(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure authorizes steps to deliver possession where the person in possession is bound by the decree. Order 21, Rule 97(1) permits the decree-holder to complain of resistance by any person, and Rule 97(2), read with Rules 98 to 103, provides for adjudication. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder is seeking delivery of immovable property under a possession decree.
predicates.obstruction_by_person: A person resists or obstructs delivery of the property.
predicates.obstructor_not_bound_by_decree: The person resisting delivery is not bound by the possession decree.

issues.definition: When a person not bound by a possession decree obstructs its execution, the obstruction is subject to an enquiry in the execution proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: Each distinct occasion of resistance to delivery of immovable property in execution gives the decree-holder a cause of action to seek removal of that resistance.
material_facts: The decree-holder encountered resistance while seeking possession under a final decree.
The resistance was attributed to a person other than the judgment-debtor.
issues.conclusion: Each occasion of obstruction or resistance furnishes a cause of action for an application seeking its removal.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21, Rule 97(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure allows the holder of a possession decree to apply when any person resists or obstructs the obtaining of possession; the court stated that each occasion of resistance furnishes a cause of action.

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder is seeking delivery of immovable property under a possession decree.
predicates.distinct_occasions_of_resistance: Resistance to obtaining possession occurs on more than one distinct occasion.

issues.definition: When resistance occurs on distinct occasions during execution of a possession decree, each occurrence supports an application to seek removal of that resistance.

issues.legal_issue: An application whose substance complains of obstruction to execution must be treated according to that substance even if it is filed under an inapplicable procedural label.
material_facts: The decree-holder filed an application seeking assistance to remove an obstruction to delivery of possession, but described it as an application under the summary delivery procedure.
The executing court directed the decree-holder to file a fresh application under the obstruction procedure.
A later application was dismissed as time-barred, and a further application was dismissed as barred by res judicata.
The initial application had been made against the person obstructing delivery.
issues.conclusion: The initial application had to be treated as an application for adjudication of the obstruction. The executing court was required to examine its averments and apply the relevant procedure; the later applications could not be rejected on limitation or res judicata grounds in the circumstances. An enquiry into the obstruction was directed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21, Rule 97(1) and (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for a complaint and adjudication of resistance to possession. The executing court must consider the averments and the applicable rule rather than treat the application’s label as controlling. The court applied the principle that procedure is the handmaid of substantive justice and relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: execution_of_possession_decree and application_complains_of_obstruction and application_mislabeled_under_summary_delivery_procedure and court_directed_fresh_application

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder is seeking delivery of immovable property under a possession decree.
predicates.application_complains_of_obstruction: The application’s substance asks the court to address a person’s resistance to delivery of possession.
predicates.application_mislabeled_under_summary_del: The applicant describes the obstruction complaint as one under a procedure intended for delivery against a person bound by the decree.
predicates.court_directed_fresh_application: The executing court directs the applicant to file a separate application under the procedure for adjudicating resistance.

issues.definition: If an application in execution substantively complains of obstruction but is filed under the wrong procedural label and the court directs a fresh filing, the initial application must be treated as an obstruction application and adjudicated.
